1.

In this revision, the revisionists has challenged the order of Ld. Trial Court, dated 12.11.2021,
passed in the case titled as "State Vs. Sajid & Ors."

bearing FIR No. 392/2012, PS Pandav Nagar,
whereby it was held that charge under Section Sajid & Anr. Vs. State & Anr. Page no.1 of 8 498A/304A/34 IPC is made out against respondent no.1 namely Sajid and charge under Section 498A/34 IPC is made out against respondent no.2 namely Abrar.

entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
2. Shorn of unnecessary details, alleged facts of the case are that on 02.09.2012, when the deceased Rubina was admitted at LNJP Hospital for treatment, she stated, in presence of the concerned SDM,
that on 27.10.2007, her marriage was solemnized with respondent no.1 namely Sajid.
She stated that after the marriage, whenever she used to visit her parental home, her in-laws including the respondents used to stop her from such visits and also used to beat her up.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She stated that her in-laws including the respondents failed to provide her proper medical treatment, whenever she used to fall sick, due to which, her medical condition deteriorated.
She also stated that her in-laws including the respondents used to ask her father to give a motorcycle, whenever her father used to visit her matrimonial home.

On 27.08.2012, when the father of the deceased had gone to her matrimonial home for bringing her to her parental home, her in-laws including the respondents started fighting with him and did not let him come back.
Lastly, at 12.00 mid night, they let them go but took her son and did not let her to take her clothes.
On 16.09.2012, during the treatment, the deceased had died.

3. It was argued by the counsel for the revisionists that in the instant case, no specific allegations have been levelled in the Sajid & Anr. Vs. State & Anr. Page no.2 of 8 complaint and only general allegations have been levelled by the complainant.
He argued that in her complaint, even the alleged role of the accused persons have not been mentioned.

He further argued that in her complaint, the deceased alleged that the respondents failed to provide her proper medical treatment, however, on the record, several medical documents are available,
showing that the deceased was treated at various hospitals.

He also argued that the final report was filed only under Section 498A/406/34 IPC but the impugned order was passed without considering the aforesaid aspect and therefore, it may be set aside.
4.
Per contra, Ld. Addl. PP for the State/respondent no.1 and counsel for the respondent no.2 argued that the impugned order is correct and needs no interference.
5. I have heard the arguments and have also gone through the Trial Court Record.

6. It is well settled that at the stage of framing the charge, the court is not supposed to marshal the evidence and it has to only see if there exists a grave suspicion against the accused for the commission of the alleged offence on the basis of the material available on the record.
Sajid & Anr. Vs. State & Anr. Page no.3 of 8 7.

In State of Maharashtra & Ors. Vs. Som Nath Thapa & Ors, AIR 1996 SC 1744, it was observed by Hon'ble Apex Court that if the court were to think that the accused might have committed the offence it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be that the accused has committed the offence.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra & Ors. Vs. Som Nath Thapa & Ors, AIR 1996 SC 1744
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is apparent that at the stage of framing of charge, probative value of the materials on record cannot be gone into and the materials brought on record by the prosecution has to be accepted as true at that stage.

Sajid And Ors vs The State on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188086437/
2 8.

entities.text: Sajid And Ors vs The State on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, in the State of Rajasthan Vs. Fatehkaran Mehdu, (2017) 3 SCC 198, Hon'ble Apex Court has held that at the stage of framing of charge, the court is concerned not with the proof of the allegation rather it has to focus on the material and form an opinion whether there is strong suspicion that the accused has committed an offence, which if put to trial, could prove his guilt.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan Vs. Fatehkaran Mehdu, (2017) 3 SCC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The framing of charge is not a stage, at which stage the final test of guilt is to be applied.

Thus, to hold that at the stage of framing the charge, the court should form an opinion that the accused is certainly guilty of committing an offence, is to hold something which is neither permissible nor is in consonance with the scheme of Code of Criminal Procedure.

9. Moreover, in Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Another, (2012) 9 SCC 460, Hon'ble Apex Court also held that no meticulous examination of the evidence is needed for considering whether the case would end in conviction or not at the stage of framing of charge or quashing of charge.

entities.text: Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Another, (2012) 9 SCC 460
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Another Sajid & Anr. Vs. State & Anr. Page no.4 of 8 very significant caution that the courts have to observe is that it cannot examine the facts, evidence and materials on record to determine whether there is sufficient material on the basis of which the case would end in a conviction; the Court is concerned primarily with the allegations taken as a whole whether they will constitute an offence and, if so, is it an abuse of the process of court leading to injustice.
Where the offence is even broadly satisfied, the Court should be more inclined to permit continuation of prosecution rather than its quashing at that initial stage.
The Court is not expected to marshal the records with a view to decide admissibility and reliability of the documents or records but a prima facie opinion has to be formed.

10. In Asim Shariff vs. National Investigating Agency, (2019) 7 SCC 148, it was held by Hon'ble Apex Court that it is expected from the trial Judge to exercise its judicial mind to determine as to whether a case for trial has been made out or not.

entities.text: Asim Shariff vs. National Investigating Agency, (2019) 7 SCC 148
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But at the same time, it also held that it is true that in such proceedings, the Court is not supposed to hold a mini trial by marshalling the evidence on record.

11. In Mahendra Prasad Tiwari vs. Amit Kumar Tiwari and Ors, Crl. Appeal No. 1210/2022 decided by Hon'ble Apex Court on 12.08.2022, it was held that the truthfulness, the sufficiency and acceptability of the material produced at the time of framing of a charge can be done only at the stage of trial and at the stage of charge the Court is to examine the materials only with a view Sajid &
Anr. Vs. State & Anr. Page no.5 of 8 to be satisfied that prima facie case of commission of offence alleged has been made out against the accused person.
12.

entities.text: Mahendra Prasad Tiwari vs. Amit Kumar Tiwari and Ors, Crl. Appeal No. 1210/2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, in her statement, the deceased had categorically stated that her in-laws including the respondents used to beat her frequently whenever, she used to visit her parental home and whenever her father used to visit her matrimonial home, they used ask him for a motorcycle.
It was also stated by her that her in-laws including the respondents failed to provide her proper medical treatment due to which her condition deteriorated.
13. It is pertinent to mention that the deceased had come from her matrimonial home in the intervening night of 27.08.2012- 28.08.2012 and on 29.08.2012, she was admitted at LNJP Hospital.
This fact prima facie shows that her medical condition was not good and probably she was not being provided proper medical treatment, as stated by her.

sentences.text: Apart from this, in his complaint made to the concerned SHO, father of the deceased alleged that when he failed to give motorcycle to the in-laws of the deceased, they started beating the deceased and stopped giving her food due to which the deceased suffered from tuberculosis.

It is further mentioned therein that when the father of the deceased got the deceased admitted in the hospital, the respondents got her discharged threatening that if she would not be sent with them,
then respondent Sajid would divorce her.
The Sajid & Anr. Vs. State & Anr. Page no.6 of 8
same conduct was again repeated by the respondents, when the father of the deceased again got the deceased admitted in the hospital.

15. Apart from this, in his complaint, the father of the deceased has mentioned that on 26.07.2012,
the deceased had called him stating that her in-laws would kill her and requested him to take her to his house.

Even, in his complaint, the father of the deceased mentioned that if the deceased would die, then her in-laws including the respondents would be responsible for her death because they did not provide her proper medical treatment.

16. Therefore, from the complaint of the father of the deceased, it is clear that even prior to the death of the deceased, he was apprehensive of the death of the deceased because despite her poor medical condition, her in-laws including the respondents did not provide her proper medical treatment and they did not even provide her food.

17. Apart from this, allegedly, when the deceased was admitted in hospital by his father on various occasions, the respondents used to get her discharged from the hospital threatening that respondent no.1 would divorce her if she failed to accompany him to her matrimonial home.

The aforesaid conduct of the respondents amounts to rash and negligent because they were allegedly aware of the fact that Sajid & Anr. Vs. State & Anr. Page no.7 of 8 the deceased was suffering from tuberculosis and if she would not be given proper food and medical treatment, she would die.

18. Perusal of the aforesaid statements of the deceased and her father along with the statements of witnesses namely Sitara, Aslam, Nasruddin, Mohd. Akbar and Nizam, shows that on the basis of the material available on the record, prima facie case of the commission of alleged offence is made out against the respondents.
19. Therefore, this court finds that the impugned order is correct and does not suffer from any illegality or impropriety and hence, needs no interference.
Accordingly, the revision stands dismissed.
20. Nothing said herein above, shall, however, be construed as any expression of opinion on the merits of the case.
21. TCR be sent back along with a copy of this order.
File be consigned to record room, as per rules.
